info.title: Flashduty Open API
info.description: Public HTTP API for the Flashduty incident management platform — incidents, notification templates, channels, schedules, monitors, RUM, and platform administration. Every operation is authenticated with an `app_key` query parameter created in the Flashduty console under My → APP Key (or sent in the `Fd-App-Key` header). Responses follow a uniform envelope: `{ request_id, data }` on success, `{ request_id, error }` on failure.

post.description: Change the evaluation order of a channel's escalation rules by moving one rule into another rule's slot.

x-mint.content:
## Restrictions

| Aspect | Value |
| ------ | ----- |
| Rate limits | **300 requests/minute**; **20 requests/second** per account |
| Permissions | **Channels Manage** (`on-call`) |

## Usage

- Rules are evaluated in ascending `priority`: the first enabled rule whose `time_filters` and `filters` match a new incident takes it, and later rules are skipped. This endpoint moves `drag_rule_id` into `target_rule_id`'s slot and renumbers the channel's rules from priority 0, changing that evaluation order.
- Both `drag_rule_id` and `target_rule_id` must be rules of `channel_id`; otherwise `InvalidParameter`.
- An unknown `channel_id` returns `InvalidParameter`.
- Concurrent reorders of the same channel are rejected with `TooManyRequests`.
- The caller must also be able to edit the channel: the account owner or an admin, the channel creator, or a member of its managing teams (of its owning team when `managing_team_ids` is empty). Otherwise the call returns `AccessDenied`.
- Every call is recorded in the account audit log.

x-mint.content:
## Restrictions

| Aspect | Value |
| ------ | ----- |
| Rate limits | **300 requests/minute**; **20 requests/second** per account |
| Permissions | **Integrations Manage** (`on-call`) |

## Usage

- Only the fields you send are changed; omitted fields keep their current value.
- Submitting `settings` replaces the configuration; known sensitive fields omitted or sent as `******` retain their value. Keeping a stored secret while changing where it is sent (such as `endpoint`, `url`, a database host or port, or an IM API base URL) is rejected, so send the secrets again with the new destination; `******` on a field with no stored value is rejected too. Send `headers: {}` to clear headers; use the integration type’s explicit empty value to clear a body.
- Submit `settings` together with `is_test: true` to receive a plugin test result; secrets in the returned settings are masked the same way.
- If another request changes the same integration's settings while this one is being processed, the call returns `RequestLocked`; retry it. A type no longer included in the account's plan returns `NoLicense`.
- These APIs manage public (account-level) integrations only, not channel-owned dedicated integrations.
- Write access also requires object permission: the account owner, an administrator, the creator, or a member of the assigned team; with no team, members with Integrations Manage may operate. Read-only integrations cannot be changed.
- Every call is recorded in the account audit log.

post.description: Return incident and alert metrics grouped by team, one row per team per time bucket.

x-mint.content:
## Restrictions

| Aspect | Value |
| ------ | ----- |
| Rate limits | **1,000 requests/minute**; **50 requests/second** per account |
| Permissions | **Analytics Read** (`on-call`) |

## Usage

- One row per team per time bucket. Incidents without a team are aggregated into a row that has no `team_id`. `responder_ids` and `incident_ids` are ignored.
- Incidents are counted by creation time. Rows are sorted by `ts` from newest to oldest, and a bucket (or dimension value) with no incidents produces no row — missing rows mean zero. `split_hours: true` returns up to three rows per bucket, one per `hours` value.
- `total_alert_cnt`, `total_alert_event_cnt` and `noise_reduction_pct` honor only the time range, team, channel and severity filters; `query`, `labels`, `fields` and the duration filters apply to incident metrics only.
- Members who are neither the account owner nor an admin only get data from channels they can access; other channels are silently excluded.
- With `is_my_team: true`, `team_ids` is narrowed to the caller's teams. If none of the sent `team_ids` is one of the caller's teams, or the caller belongs to no team, the result is empty.

post.description: Export channel insight metrics as a CSV file with the same rows as `/insight/channel`.

x-mint.content:
## Restrictions

| Aspect | Value |
| ------ | ----- |
| Rate limits | **100 requests/day**; **20 requests/minute**; **10 requests/second** per account |
| Permissions | **Analytics Read** (`on-call`) |

## Usage

- The response is a CSV file (`Content-Type: application/octet-stream`), not a JSON envelope. Validation errors are returned as JSON before any CSV bytes are written.
- Takes the same filters as `/insight/channel`. Rows without a channel ID are skipped. The file has no time-bucket column, so with `aggregate_unit` the rows of different buckets cannot be told apart; export one bucket per request if you need the split.
- `export_fields` sets the columns and their order: channel_id, channel_name, total_incident_cnt, total_incidents_acknowledged, total_incidents_closed, total_incidents_auto_closed, total_incidents_manually_closed, total_incidents_timeout_closed, total_incidents_escalated, total_incidents_manually_escalated, total_incidents_timeout_escalated, total_incidents_reassigned, total_interruptions, total_notifications, total_engaged_seconds, mean_seconds_to_ack, mean_seconds_to_close, noise_reduction_pct, acknowledgement_pct, total_alert_cnt, total_alert_event_cnt, hours. Unknown or duplicate keys are rejected. When it is omitted, all columns are exported, and `hours` is included only when `split_hours` is true.
- The incident-snapshot keys (progress, assigned_to, raw_assigned_to, escalate_rule_name, responders, raw_responders, ackers, owner_id, owner_name, creator_id, creator_name, closer_id, closer_name, snooze_status, snoozed_before, ever_muted, frequency, is_rare, alert_cnt, active_alert_cnt, alert_event_cnt, description, labels, fields) are also accepted for compatibility and produce empty columns.
- Column headers are localized (request locale, then the member's, then the account's). Time buckets follow `time_zone` (UTC when omitted).

post.description: Set the alert processing pipeline for an integration. Replaces the existing configuration entirely.

x-mint.content:
## Restrictions

| Aspect | Value |
| ------ | ----- |
| Rate limits | **300 requests/minute**; **20 requests/second** per account |
| Permissions | **Channels Manage** (`on-call`) or **Integrations Manage** (`on-call`) |

## Usage

- Replaces the integration's whole rule list with `rules`; an empty array removes every rule. At most 50 rules.
- Rules run in array order on each incoming event of the integration before it becomes an alert; `alert_drop`, or an `alert_inhibit` that matches, discards the event and stops processing.
- `integration_id` may be an account-level or a channel-owned integration; an ID not in the account returns `InvalidParameter`.
- Write access also requires object permission: the account owner, an administrator, the integration creator, or a member of its team (for a channel-owned integration, a member of the channel's team); with no team, any caller with the API permission may write.
- An `alert_inhibit` rule requires the Standard plan or higher; otherwise the call returns `NoLicense`.
- On success the response carries only `request_id`; the `data` field is omitted.
- Every call is recorded in the account audit log. Don't put secrets in request fields.

post.description: Close one or more incidents, optionally recording root cause, resolution, and resolution form values.

x-mint.content:
## Restrictions

| Aspect | Value |
| ------ | ----- |
| Rate limits | **300 requests/minute**; **20 requests/second** per account |
| Permissions | **Incidents Manage** or **Channels Manage** (`on-call`) |

## Usage

- When a resolution form applies, `custom_fields`, `summary`, and `images` must match its visible elements and required rules.
- For a batch, form values are accepted only when every selected incident resolves to the same form; otherwise resolve incidents individually.
- The legacy `values` and `custom_values` properties are rejected; use `custom_fields`.
- Incidents that are already closed are skipped without error; an unknown ID fails the whole call with `InvalidParameter`.
- Resolving a `Triggered` incident first acknowledges it on behalf of the caller.
- After closing, unfinished action items of the incident are converted to follow-ups, and later events no longer merge into the incident's existing alerts.
- Returns `RequestTooFrequently` while another resolve, reopen, merge, comment, or delete is running in the same account; retry after a short delay.

example.root_cause: Memory leak in the connection pool caused by a missing cleanup call.

post.description: Return a cursor-paginated list of alerts matching the given filters.

x-mint.content:
## Restrictions

| Aspect | Value |
| ------ | ----- |
| Rate limits | **1,000 requests/minute**; **50 requests/second** per account |
| Permissions | **Channels Read** (`on-call`) or **Channels Manage** (`on-call`) or **Incidents Read** (`on-call`) or **Incidents Manage** (`on-call`) or **Integrations Read** (`on-call`) or **Integrations Manage** (`on-call`) |

## Usage

- `start_time` and `end_time` are required Unix seconds and filter on the alert's `start_time`; the span must not exceed 31 days.
- With `by_updated_at: true`, an `updated_at` window with the same bounds is added on top of the `start_time` filter, and the span must not exceed 7 days.
- A `start_time` earlier than the account's data retention period is moved up to the retention start; an `end_time` before that start returns `InvalidParameter`.
- Pass `search_after_ctx` from the previous response for the next page; without it, `p`/`limit` page numbers apply and `p * limit` must stay within 10,000.
- `total` is capped at 1,000. `has_next_page` does not depend on `total`: it is exact in both page-number and cursor mode, also past 1,000 alerts. Every non-empty page returns `search_after_ctx` for its last alert; pass it back to read past the 10,000-row page-number limit.
- Results are filtered by the caller's channel data-access permissions.
- Set `is_active` to `true` to retrieve only active (firing) alerts; `false` to retrieve resolved alerts.

person_ids.description: Member IDs to add as responders. IDs that are already responders, or that do not exist in the account, are skipped.

notify.description: Notification settings for the newly added responders. Defaults to `{"follow_preference": true}`.

follow_preference.description: `true`: notify each person through their personal notification preference. `false`: use `personal_channels`, which must then be non-empty. When omitted, `personal_channels` must be set.

personal_channels.description: Channels used when `follow_preference` is `false`: `sms`, `voice`, `email`, `push` (mobile app push), or an IM app channel written as `feishu_app:<integration_id>`, `dingtalk_app:<integration_id>`, `wecom_app:<integration_id>`, `slack_app:<integration_id>`, or `teams_app:<integration_id>`. Ignored when `follow_preference` is `true`.

template_id.description: Notification template ID, as returned by the notification template endpoints. Must exist in the account; otherwise the call fails with `InvalidParameter`.

AffectedStatusPageComponentItem.description: A status page component currently affected by an event, embedding component metadata plus its resulting status.

section_id.description: Parent section ID. Omitted when the component sits at the top level.

name.description: Component display name.

available_since_seconds.description: Time the component became available, as a Unix timestamp in seconds. Omitted when 0.

order_id.description: Display order within its section. Omitted when 0.

hide_uptime.description: When true, uptime data is hidden from summary responses. Omitted when false.

hide_all.description: When true, the component is hidden entirely from summary endpoints. Omitted when false.

status.description:
Current status of the component affected by the change. Severity increases: `operational` < `degraded` = `under_maintenance` < `partial_outage` < `full_outage`; incident-type changes may use the first four, maintenance-type changes only `operational` and `under_maintenance`.
| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `operational` | Operating normally. |
| `degraded` | Degraded performance. |
| `partial_outage` | Partial outage. |
| `full_outage` | Full outage. |
| `under_maintenance` | Under maintenance. |

AlertEventGlobalListRequest.description: Filter and pagination criteria for the global raw event list. Time range is required.

start_time.description: Start of the search window, Unix epoch seconds. Must be greater than 0.

end_time.description: End of the search window, Unix epoch seconds. Must be greater than `start_time`; the span must not exceed 31 days.

p.description: Page number, starting at 1. Used when `search_after_ctx` is not provided.

search_after_ctx.description: Pagination cursor: leave empty for the first page, then pass the `search_after_ctx` returned by the previous response.

channel_ids.description: Filter by channel IDs. At most 100 entries. Channels the caller cannot access are dropped; if none remain, the result is empty.

severities.description: Comma-separated filter on `event_severity`, e.g. `Critical,Warning`. Meaningful values: `Critical`, `Warning`, `Info`. Values are not validated; an unknown value (or `Ok`) matches nothing.

total.description: Total number of matching events, capped at 1000.

has_next_page.description: Whether a next page exists (probed by fetching limit+1 rows).

search_after_ctx.description: Cursor for the next page — the ObjectID of the last event on this page; pass it back as `search_after_ctx`. Omitted when the page is empty; in cursor mode also omitted when there is no next page.

items.description: Raw alert events on the current page.

account_id.description: ID of the account that owns this record; the same for every record returned to one `app_key`.

channel_id.description: Channel ID the event is routed to.

integration_id.description: Integration that produced this event.

integration_type.description: Plugin type of the integration, such as `prometheus.alert`, `grafana.alert`, `zabbix.alert`, `monit.alert`, or `email.alert`. The set is open and grows with new integrations; `POST /integration/type/list` returns the full list.

title_rule.description: Title template used to derive `title` from labels.

alert_key.description: Deduplication key used to merge events into an alert.

event_severity.description: Severity of this event: `Critical`, `Warning`, or `Info`. An event never carries `Ok` as severity — `Ok` appears only as `event_status`.

event_status.description: Status carried by this event: `Critical`/`Warning`/`Info` for a firing event, `Ok` for a recovery event.

created_at.description: Record creation time, Unix epoch seconds.

updated_at.description: Record update time, Unix epoch seconds.

deleted_at.description: Soft-delete time, Unix epoch seconds. Omitted when the event is not deleted.

asc.description: When true, return events oldest-first. Defaults to newest-first.

limit.description: Page size. Defaults to 20 and cannot exceed 100.

p.description: Page number starting at 1. Used when `search_after_ctx` is omitted.

search_after_ctx.description: Cursor returned by the previous page. When supplied, cursor pagination is used instead of page-number pagination.

items.description: Raw alert events in the requested order.

total.description: Total matching event count, capped at 1000.

search_after_ctx.description: Cursor to pass as `search_after_ctx` for the next page. Omitted when the page is empty; in cursor mode also omitted when there is no next page.

alert_id.description: Alert ID (ObjectID hex string); obtain it from `POST /alert/list`.

types.description: Filter by feed type codes — see the `type` field of the response items for the full list (e.g. `a_new`, `a_comm`, `a_merge`).

items.description: Alert feed records on the current page.

AlertFeedType.description:
Alert activity feed entry type. Each value identifies one alert lifecycle event; the matching `detail` payload shape is determined by this field.

| Type | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `a_new` | Alert triggered by an incoming event. |
| `a_update` | Alert severity or status changed on an incoming event. |
| `a_comm` | Comment added on the alert. |
| `a_merge` | Alert merged into an incident. |
| `a_m_silence` | Alert muted by a silence rule. |
| `a_m_inhibit` | Alert muted by an inhibit rule. |
| `a_m_flapping` | Alert muted by flapping detection (historical data only; no longer produced). |
| `a_ack` | Alert acknowledged (historical data only; alert-level acknowledgement has been removed). |
| `a_unack` | Alert acknowledgement revoked (historical data only). |
| `a_close` | Alert closed (historical data only; no longer produced). |

AlertImage.description: An image attachment on an alert or event.

href.description: Optional link URL when the image is clicked.

src.description: Image source URL or internal image reference (starts with `img_` or `http`).

alt.description: Alternative text shown when the image cannot be displayed; empty when not set.

integration_id.description: Integration ID that produced the alert.

channel_id.description: ID of the channel the alert was routed to; its name is in `channel_name`.

account_id.description: ID of the account that owns this record; the same for every record returned to one `app_key`.

alert_key.description: Deduplication key used to merge events into the alert.

start_time.description: Unix timestamp (seconds) when the alert first fired.

last_time.description: Unix timestamp (seconds) of the most recent event.

end_time.description: Unix timestamp (seconds) when the alert recovered. 0 if still active.

ever_muted.description: Whether this alert has ever been silenced.

deleted_at.description: Soft-delete timestamp (seconds). Zero if not deleted.

created_at.description: Creation timestamp (seconds).

updated_at.description: Last update timestamp (seconds).

integration_type.description: Plugin type of the integration, such as `prometheus.alert`, `grafana.alert`, `zabbix.alert`, `monit.alert`, or `email.alert`. The set is open and grows with new integrations; `POST /integration/type/list` returns the full list.

channel_status.description: Status of the channel: `enabled`, `disabled`, or `deleted`. Empty string when the record has no channel or the channel no longer exists.

responder_name.description: Always an empty string in API responses; filled only when the alert is rendered for notifications.

responder_email.description: Always an empty string in API responses; filled only when the alert is rendered for notifications.

incident.description: Parent incident reference, if the alert has been merged into one.

events.description: Raw alert event preview, populated only when requested. Capped at the 20 newest events per alert.

event_cnt.description: Total number of raw events merged into this alert.

images.description: Images attached to the alert; `null` when there are none.

detail_url.description: Console URL of this alert (`{console}/alert/detail/{alert_id}`). Empty when the deployment has no console base configured.

AlertItem.description: A single alert with full detail.

integration_id.description: ID of the integration that produced this alert.

channel_id.description: ID of the channel the alert belongs to.

account_id.description: ID of the account that owns the alert.

title_rule.description: Title template used to derive `title` from the event labels (e.g. `$service::$cluster`).

alert_severity.description: Current severity — the highest severity ever seen on this alert: `Critical`, `Warning`, or `Info`.

alert_status.description: Current status: `Critical`/`Warning`/`Info` while firing, `Ok` once recovered.

end_time.description: Resolution time, Unix epoch seconds. 0 if still active.

labels.description: Label key-value pairs; `null` when the alert has no labels.

ever_muted.description: True if this alert has ever been silenced.

created_at.description: Creation timestamp, Unix epoch seconds.

updated_at.description: Last update timestamp, Unix epoch seconds.

integration_type.description: Type key of the integration that produced the alert, e.g. `prometheus.alert` or `zabbix.alert`; same values as `plugin_type` from `POST /integration/type/list`.

integration_ref_id.description: Owner reference of the integration: `a_<account_id>` for an account-level integration, `c_<channel_id>` for a channel-owned one.

responder_name.description: Responder display name. Always empty in this response — responder tracking lives on the associated incident.

responder_email.description: Responder email. Always empty in this response — responder tracking lives on the associated incident.

event_cnt.description: Total number of raw events received by this alert.

events.description: Raw events of this alert. Omitted here; populated only by `POST /incident/alert/list`.

images.description: Images attached to the alert; `null` when there are none.

detail_url.description: Console URL of this alert (`{console}/alert/detail/{alert_id}`). Empty when the deployment has no console base configured.

data_source_type.description: Deprecated: use `integration_type` instead (same value, e.g. `prometheus.alert`). Omitted when empty.

deleted_at.description: Soft-delete time, Unix epoch seconds. Omitted when the alert is not deleted.

alert_ids.description: Alert IDs (ObjectID hex strings) to fetch. A malformed ID fails the request; IDs not found in the account are left out of the result.

AlertListRequest.description: Filter and pagination criteria for alert list queries. Time range is required.

start_time.description: Start of the search window, Unix epoch seconds, applied to the alert's `start_time`. A value earlier than the account's data retention period is moved up to the retention start.

end_time.description: End of the search window, Unix epoch seconds. Must be greater than `start_time`; the span must not exceed 31 days (7 days with `by_updated_at`). A value before the start of the data retention period returns `InvalidParameter`.

p.description: Page number, starting at 1. Used when `search_after_ctx` is not provided; `p * limit` must stay within 10,000 records.

search_after_ctx.description: Opaque cursor from the previous response for the next page.

is_active.description: Filter by lifecycle: `true` returns only firing alerts (status `Critical`/`Warning`/`Info`), `false` returns only recovered alerts (status `Ok`). Omit or pass `null` to return both.

ever_muted.description: Filter by whether the alert has ever been silenced.

alert_severity.description: Comma-separated filter on `alert_severity`, e.g. `Critical,Warning`. Allowed values: `Critical`, `Warning`, `Info`, `Ok`; other values return `InvalidParameter`. `Ok` matches nothing because `alert_severity` is never `Ok`.

alert_ids.description: Filter to specific alert IDs (ObjectID hex strings). Invalid IDs are ignored; if none are valid, the result is empty.

asc.description: Sort ascending by `start_time` when `true`; default is descending.

by_updated_at.description: When `true`, also require the alert's `updated_at` to fall within [`start_time`, `end_time`], in addition to the `start_time` filter; the span must then not exceed 7 days.

total.description: Number of matching alerts, capped at 1,000.

has_next_page.description: `true` when another page exists. Exact in both cursor mode (`search_after_ctx` sent) and page-number mode, including past the 1,000 cap of `total`.

search_after_ctx.description: Cursor for the next page — the ObjectID hex of the last alert on this page; pass it back as `search_after_ctx`. Omitted when the page is empty; in cursor mode also omitted when there is no next page.

items.description: Alerts on the current page.

alert_ids.description: Alert IDs to merge (ObjectID hex strings); obtain them from `POST /alert/list`. Every ID must belong to the caller's account.

incident_id.description: Target incident ID (ObjectID hex string); obtain it from `POST /incident/list`.

comment.description: Optional comment recorded on the merge feed entry. At most 1024 characters.

title.description: Optional new title for the target incident. At most 512 characters.

owner_id.description: Member ID of the new owner for the target incident; obtain it from `POST /member/list`.

kind.description:
Rule type. Rules run in array order; when the `if` condition matches, the event is processed according to `kind`.
| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `title_reset` | Rewrites the event title from the `settings.title` template. |
| `description_reset` | Rewrites the event description from the `settings.description` template. |
| `severity_reset` | Resets the event severity and status to `settings.severity` (`Critical`/`Warning`/`Info`). |
| `alert_drop` | Discards the matching event outright; no alert is created. |
| `alert_inhibit` | Discards the event (inhibition) when an active source alert matching `settings.source_filters` and correlated via `settings.equals` exists. |

if.description: AND-filter list — the rule applies only when every condition matches the incoming event. Keys: `severity` (aliases `alert_severity`, `event_severity`), `status`, `title`, `title_rule`, `description`, `alert_key`, `integration_id` (alias `data_source_id`), and `labels.<name>`; other keys return `InvalidParameter`. `null` or omitted means the rule applies to all events.

settings.description:
Kind-specific settings. Shape depends on `kind`:
- `title_reset`: `{ "title": "<string>" }`
- `description_reset`: `{ "description": "<string>" }`
- `severity_reset`: `{ "severity": "Critical"|"Warning"|"Info" }`
- `alert_drop`: `{}` (empty object)
- `alert_inhibit`: `{ "equals": ["<label_key>", ...], "source_filters": <OrFilterGroup> }`

integration_id.description: Integration ID. Must be greater than 0.

AlertPipelineItem.description: Alert processing pipeline for an integration.

integration_id.description: Integration ID this pipeline applies to.

status.description: Pipeline status. Always `enabled` in these responses — deleted pipelines are filtered out.

creator_id.description: Member ID who created the pipeline.

updated_by.description: Member ID who last updated the pipeline.

created_at.description: Creation timestamp, Unix epoch seconds.

updated_at.description: Last update timestamp, Unix epoch seconds.

deleted_at.description: Soft-delete time, Unix epoch seconds. Omitted when not deleted.

integration_ids.description: Integration IDs. At least one entry is required.

items.description: Alert pipeline configuration of each requested integration, one item per configured integration.

integration_id.description: ID of the integration to configure; account-level and channel-owned integrations are both accepted.

rules.description: Rules to apply, evaluated in array order. At most 50 entries; an empty array removes all rules.

ApAlertDrop.description: Settings for `alert_drop`: no fields; send `{}`. A matching event is discarded and no alert is created or updated.

ApAlertInhibit.description: Settings for `alert_inhibit`: the current event is discarded when an active alert of the same integration, with a different `alert_key` and started within the 10 minutes before the event, matches `source_filters` and has the same value as the event for every `equals` key.

equals.description: Keys whose values must be equal on the source alert and the current event: `title`, `severity`, or `labels.<name>`. An empty list, any other key, or a label missing on the event means the rule never inhibits.

source_filters.description: AND-conditions a source alert must meet. Allowed keys: `severity`, `title`, and `labels.<name>`; other keys return `InvalidParameter`.

ApDescriptionReset.description: Settings for `description_reset`: replaces the event description with a rendered template.

description.description: Description template. Only a value starting with `[TPL]` takes effect: the rest is rendered as a Go template against the event and replaces the description. A value without the prefix leaves the description unchanged.

ApSeverityReset.description: Settings for `severity_reset`: sets the event severity, and its status, to a fixed value.

severity.description: Severity to set: `Critical`, `Warning` or `Info`. The event status is set to the same value.

ApTitleReset.description: Settings for `title_reset`: replaces the event title using a title rule.

title.description: Title rule. A value starting with `[TPL]` is a Go template rendered against the event, e.g. `[TPL]{{.Labels.service}}`. Otherwise it is a `::`-separated list in which each `$name` part is replaced by the value of label `name` and other parts are kept as written.

AssignIncidentRequest.description: Parameters for dispatching one or more incidents to a target. Provide `incident_id` or `incident_ids` but not both.

incident_id.description: Single incident ID. Ignored when `incident_ids` is also provided.

incident_ids.description: Incident IDs to assign in bulk; obtain them from `POST /incident/list`.

assigned_to.description: Assignment target. Set `person_ids`, `escalate_rule_id`, or `emails`; when none is set, the server re-runs the channel's escalation rule matching.

AssignedTo.description: Assignment target. In requests, set `person_ids`, `escalate_rule_id`, or `emails`; when none is set the server re-runs the channel's escalation rule matching. In responses the object is always present; an incident that was never assigned has empty `type`, `id`, and `assigned_at` of `0`.

escalate_rule_id.description: Escalation rule ID (MongoDB ObjectID) to drive assignment.

layer_idx.description: Zero-based escalation level within `escalate_rule_id` (`0` = first level). Responders are taken from this level.

type.description: How the assignment happened: `assign` first assignment; `reassign` reassignment of an already assigned incident; `escalate` moved by the escalation flow; `reopen` reassignment after the incident was reopened; empty string in responses when the incident was never assigned. Omit it in requests and the server derives it.

emails.description: Member emails; each is resolved to a member ID and merged into `person_ids`. Emails without a matching member are ignored.

notify.description: Override the notification channels used for this assignment.

follow_preference.description: `true`: notify each person through their personal notification preference. `false`: use `personal_channels`, which must then be non-empty. When omitted, `personal_channels` must be set.

personal_channels.description: Channels used when `follow_preference` is `false`: `sms`, `voice`, `email`, `push` (mobile app push), or an IM app channel written as `feishu_app:<integration_id>`, `dingtalk_app:<integration_id>`, `wecom_app:<integration_id>`, `slack_app:<integration_id>`, or `teams_app:<integration_id>`. Ignored when `follow_preference` is `true`.

template_id.description: Notification template ID (MongoDB ObjectID).

escalate_rule_name.description: Escalation rule name, filled by the server in responses; ignored in requests.

assigned_at.description: Unix timestamp (seconds) when the assignment was made; set by the server.

id.description: Assignment ID generated by the server for each assignment; set by the server.

effective_person_ids.description: Member IDs that actually received the assignment: `person_ids` plus the members of the selected escalation level, deduplicated and sorted. Set by the server; omitted when empty.

CalEventIDRequest.description: Calendar event delete request. Provide event_id, or both start_at and end_at.

event_id.description: ID of the event to delete. Omit when clearing a date range.

start_at.description: Start date of the range to clear, in YYYY-MM-DD. Pass together with end_at instead of event_id.

end_at.description: End date of the range to clear, in YYYY-MM-DD (exclusive). Must be later than start_at.

account_id.description: Account ID. Only present for private events.

creator_id.description: Creator person ID. Only present for private events.

cal_id.description: Calendar ID. For public events this is a locale key such as zh-cn.china.official.

event_id.description: Event ID. `cale.<id>` for the calendar's own events, `non_work.YYYYMMDD` for generated non-working weekdays, and `<holiday cal_id>.<id>` for events inherited from a holiday calendar.

is_off.description: Whether the event marks a non-working day.

created_at.description: Creation timestamp (Unix seconds); `0` for generated `non_work.*` entries.

updated_at.description: Last update timestamp (Unix seconds); `0` for generated `non_work.*` entries.

CalEventListRequest.description: Calendar event list request. When day > 0 month must also be specified. month and day accept 0 to mean "not filtered".

year.description: Year. Defaults to the current year when omitted.

items.description: Calendar events sorted by start_at.

total.description: Total number of events returned.

days.description: Resolved state of every day in the requested scope, keyed by date (YYYY-MM-DD). The highest layer holding any event decides a day: the calendar's own events (custom), then the linked holiday calendars (holiday), then the weekly workdays (weekly). Inside one layer a working-day event beats a day off, so a make-up workday from a holiday calendar wins over holiday rest days. A day no event covers is a working day.

CalDay.description: Resolved state of one calendar day.

is_off.description: Whether the day is a day off.

event_id.description: ID of the event that decided the day. Absent when no event covers the day.

layer.description: Layer that decided the day: custom = the calendar's own events, holiday = a linked holiday calendar, weekly = the weekly workdays. Absent when no event covers the day.

CalEventUpsertRequest.description: Calendar event upsert request. Provide event_id to update an existing event; omit it to create a new one.

is_off.description: Whether the event marks a non-working day. true = day off, false = working day override.

CalendarCreateRequest.description: Create calendar request. cal_name is required.

cal_name.description: Calendar display name; must be unique within the account.

timezone.description: IANA timezone, e.g. `America/New_York`. Defaults to `Asia/Shanghai` when empty; an invalid name returns `InvalidParameter`.

team_id.description: Owning team ID; `0` or omitted means no team. A nonzero ID must be a team of the account.

workdays.description: Weekly working days, `0` = Sunday … `6` = Saturday. Days not listed are non-working days. When empty, no weekday is treated as non-working.

extra_cal_ids.description: Additional public-holiday calendar IDs to inherit events from (for example zh-cn.china.official).

cal_id.description: ID of the newly created calendar (format cal.<uuid>).

CalendarIDRequest.description: Request body carrying a calendar ID.

account_id.description: ID of the account that owns the calendar.

team_id.description: Owning team ID (0 when not assigned).

kind.description: Calendar kind. `region.official.holiday` is a public regional holiday calendar (served by the central holiday service), `religion.holiday` is a public religious holiday calendar (reserved, currently no data), and `personal` is an account-created personal/team calendar.

workdays.description: Weekly working days, `0` = Sunday … `6` = Saturday. Days not listed are non-working days. When empty, no weekday is treated as non-working. Omitted when empty.

extra_cal_ids.description: Inherited public-holiday calendar IDs. Omitted when empty.

created_at.description: Creation timestamp (Unix seconds).

updated_at.description: Last update timestamp (Unix seconds).

creator_id.description: Creator person ID.

status.description: Calendar status. `enabled` means usable; `deleted` means removed and never returned by list endpoints.

CalendarListRequest.description: Calendar list request. kind filters by calendar kind; no_locale disables locale filtering for public holiday calendars.

kind.description: Calendar kind filter; defaults to personal when empty. `region.official.holiday` queries public regional holiday calendars (filtered by the caller's locale); `personal` queries account-created calendars.

no_locale.description: Disable locale filtering when listing public-holiday calendars.

items.description: Calendar items.

total.description: Total number of calendars returned.

CalendarUpdateRequest.description: Update calendar request. cal_id is required; all other fields are optional and only applied when provided.

cal_name.description: New calendar name; must be unique within the account.

timezone.description: New IANA timezone, e.g. `Asia/Shanghai`; an invalid name returns `InvalidParameter`.

team_id.description: New owning team ID; obtain it from `POST /team/list`. `0` removes the team; a nonzero ID must be a team of the account.

workdays.description: Weekly working days, `0` = Sunday … `6` = Saturday. Days not listed are non-working days. When empty, no weekday is treated as non-working. When sent, replaces the stored list; omit to keep it.

extra_cal_ids.description: Public holiday calendar IDs to inherit events from (see `POST /calendar/list` with `kind` = `region.official.holiday`). When sent, replaces the stored list; an empty array removes them all; omit to keep it.

CancelStatusPageMigrationRequest.description: Parameters for cancelling an in-progress migration job.

job_id.description: Migration job ID, returned when the migration job is created; check progress via `GET /status-page/migration/status`.

channel_id.description: Newly created channel ID.

channel_name.description: Channel name echoed back from the request.

external_report_token.description: Token for external reporters. Returned only when the request set `is_external_report_enabled` to `true`; it can be read again later from `POST /channel/info`.

channel_id.description: Channel ID; obtain it from `POST /channel/list`.
ID of the channel to query; obtain it from `POST /channel/list`.

channel_ids.description: Channel IDs to look up. Up to 1000.

items.description: Requested channels that exist, including deleted ones; unknown IDs are skipped. Ordered by channel creation, not by request order.

ChannelItem.description: Channel detail record. All fields are optional; they are emitted only when populated.

channel_id.description: Channel ID; pass it as `channel_id` to the other channel and rule endpoints.

team_id.description: Owning team ID.

team_name.description: Owning team name, resolved from the team directory. Returned only by `POST /channel/list` without `is_brief`; omitted when the lookup fails.

managing_team_ids.description: Additional teams that can manage the channel.

creator_id.description: Member ID who created the channel.

creator_name.description: Name of the member who created the channel. Returned only by `POST /channel/list` without `is_brief`; omitted when the lookup fails.

account_id.description: Owning account ID.

channel_name.description: Channel name, unique within the account, 1–59 characters.

status.description:
Channel status:
- `enabled`: incoming alert events are processed.
- `disabled`: incoming alert events are discarded.
- `deleted`: the channel was deleted; returned only by `POST /channel/info` and `POST /channel/infos`, never by `POST /channel/list`.

deleted_at.description: Deletion time, Unix timestamp in seconds. Non-zero only for soft-deleted channels.

created_at.description: Creation time, Unix timestamp in seconds.

updated_at.description: Last update time, Unix timestamp in seconds.

auto_resolve_timeout.description: Auto-resolve timeout in seconds. 0 disables auto-resolve.

auto_resolve_mode.description: How the auto-resolve timer is reset. `trigger` (default) starts the timer once when the incident is triggered — later merged alerts do not affect it; `update` restarts the timer from the latest alert time whenever a new alert merges into the incident.

is_private.description: When true, the channel is visible only to its managing teams.

disable_outlier_detection.description: When true, outlier incident detection is disabled.

disable_auto_close.description: When true, automatic incident closing is disabled.

group.description: Alert grouping configuration. When never set, `{"method": "n"}` (no grouping) is returned.

flapping.description: Flapping detection configuration. When never set, the defaults are returned: enabled, 4 changes within 60 minutes, muted for 120 minutes.

progress_to_incident_cnts.description: Counts of incidents started in the last 30 days that are still open, by progress. Not returned with `is_brief`.

is_starred.description: Whether the caller has starred this channel. Returned only by `POST /channel/list`.

active_incident_highest_severity.description: Highest severity among the channel's active (triggered or processing) incidents: `Critical`, `Warning` or `Info`. Omitted when there are no active incidents.

last_incident_at.description: Time of the most recent incident, Unix timestamp in seconds.

is_external_report_enabled.description: Whether external reporters can file incidents into this channel.

external_report_token.description: Token external reporters use to file incidents into this channel. Returned only when external reporting is enabled.

event_group.description: Alert event merge configuration. When never set, merging is enabled with a 1,440-minute window.

channel_id.description: Owning channel ID; obtain it from `POST /channel/list`.

rule_id.description: Rule ID (24-character hex), as returned in `rule_id` by the create or list endpoint of the same rule type.

channel_id.description: Channel whose rules to list; obtain it from `POST /channel/list`.
Channel ID, one of the requested `channel_ids`.

channel_name.description: Channel name, unique within the account.

status.description:
Channel status:
- `enabled`: incoming alert events are processed.
- `disabled`: incoming alert events are discarded.
- `deleted`: the channel was deleted.

CommentIncidentRequest.description: Parameters for adding a comment to one or more incidents.

incident_ids.description: Incident IDs to comment on. At most 100 per call.

comment.description: Comment body. Leading and trailing whitespace is trimmed; the comment must be non-empty after trimming and at most 1024 characters (counted after @mention normalization).

mute_reply.description: When true, do not trigger webhook reply actions for this comment.

comment_type_id.description: Optional ID of an account-level comment type to attach to the comment (MongoDB ObjectID). An invalid or all-zero ID is rejected with 400.

team_id.description: Owning team ID; obtain it from `POST /team/list`. Required and must exist.

managing_team_ids.description: Additional teams that can manage the channel. Up to 3 entries.

channel_name.description: Channel name, 1–59 characters, unique within the account.

escalate_rule.description: Creates an enabled escalation rule named `Default` with a single level that notifies `target` once. Omit to create the channel without escalation rules.

aggr_window.description: Delay in seconds, 0–3600, before the first notification for a newly assigned incident; `0` notifies immediately.

template_id.description: Notification template ID (24-character hex); obtain it from `POST /template/list`. Must exist.

target.description: Who to notify and through which channels.

group.description: Alert grouping configuration. Omit for no grouping (`method` `n`).

flapping.description: Flapping detection configuration. Omit to use the defaults.

auto_resolve_timeout.description: Auto-resolve timeout in seconds. 0 disables auto-resolve. Max 30 days.

auto_resolve_mode.description: How the auto-resolve timer runs. `trigger` (default) starts the timer once when the incident is triggered; `update` restarts it whenever a new alert merges into the incident.

plugin_ids.description: Integration type IDs (the `plugin_id` shown on integrations returned by `POST /integration/list`). For each ID, a channel-exclusive integration of that type is created, named after the type. An unknown ID returns `InvalidParameter`.

is_private.description: When true, the channel is visible only to its managing teams.

is_external_report_enabled.description: When true, external reporters can file incidents into this channel, and the response carries the generated `external_report_token`.

event_group.description: Alert event merge configuration. Omit to use the default (merge enabled, 1440-minute window).

CreateDropRuleRequest.description: Parameters for creating a channel drop rule.

channel_id.description: Owning channel ID; obtain it from `POST /channel/list`.

filters.description: Alert event conditions (OR of AND groups). A matching event is discarded entirely: no alert, incident or notification. Keys: `title`, `description`, `severity` (alias `alert_severity`, `event_severity`), `status`, `alert_key`, `title_rule`, `integration_id` (alias `data_source_id`), or any `labels.<name>`. When omitted or empty, the rule matches nothing.

CreateEscalationRuleRequest.description: Parameters for creating an escalation rule.

channel_id.description: Owning channel ID; obtain it from `POST /channel/list`.

priority.description: Evaluation order from `0` to `200`; lower values are evaluated first. Omit to place the rule after all existing rules (current highest priority + 1).

aggr_window.description: Delay in seconds, 0–3600, before the first notification for a newly assigned incident; `0` notifies immediately.

template_id.description: Notification template ID (24-character hex); obtain it from `POST /template/list`. Must exist.

layers.description: Escalation levels in order; the incident starts at the first level.

time_filters.description: Recurring time windows during which the rule can match; omit or leave empty to match at any time.

filters.description: Incident conditions (OR of AND groups), matched against the incident the alert was grouped into, not against the alert. Keys: `title`, `description`, `severity` (alias `incident_severity`, `alert_severity`), `status` (alias `incident_status`, `alert_status`), `dedup_key`, `integration_id` (alias `data_source_id`), or any `labels.<name>`. Omit or leave empty to match every incident in the channel.

CreateIncidentRequest.description: Parameters for manually creating an incident.

title.description: Incident title, up to 512 characters. Required (non-blank) when the account has a create form.

channel_id.description: Channel to file the incident into; must exist in the account. Optional unless the account has a create form; leave it unset for a standalone incident.

assigned_to.description: Who to assign. When omitted or empty, the channel's escalation rules decide (a standalone incident gets no responders); required when the account has a create form. `person_ids`, `escalate_rule_id` and `emails` can be combined — responders are the union. Assignment runs after creation, and its failure does not undo the incident.

person_ids.description: Member IDs to assign directly (1–100). Can be combined with `escalate_rule_id`.

escalate_rule_id.description: Escalation rule ID (MongoDB ObjectID); assigns the people at the rule's `layer_idx` layer.

layer_idx.description: Zero-based escalation-rule layer to assign (default 0, the first layer). Used only with `escalate_rule_id`; an out-of-range value leaves the incident without responders instead of failing the request.

type.description:
Assignment type. Normally omitted: the server then sets `assign`, because a manual create is always a first assignment. A value you send is stored as-is.
- `assign`: first assignment of the incident.
- `reassign`: assignment replacing an earlier one.
- `escalate`: assignment triggered by escalation to the next layer.
- `reopen`: assignment restarted from the first layer after the incident is reopened.

emails.description: Recipients to assign by email (1–100): resolved to account members and merged into `person_ids`; emails with no matching member are ignored.

notify.description: Override the notification channels used for this assignment.

follow_preference.description: When false, use `personal_channels`; when true or omitted, use each responder's personal preference.

personal_channels.description: Channels to use when `follow_preference` is false: `sms`, `voice`, `email`, `push`, or an IM app channel prefixed `feishu_app:`, `dingtalk_app:`, `wecom_app:`, `slack_app:` or `teams_app:`.

template_id.description: Notification template ID (MongoDB ObjectID).

fields.description: Custom field values keyed by field name. When a create form applies, only its visible fields are accepted.

labels.description: Labels to store on the created incident, up to 50 entries. Blank values are dropped. Spaces and selected punctuation in keys become `_`; keys and values are trimmed, and values are truncated at 8 KiB.

CreateIncidentResponse.description: Result of manually creating an incident.

title.description: Incident title as sent in the request; empty when the request had no title.

CreateInhibitRuleRequest.description: Parameters for creating an inhibit rule.

channel_id.description: Owning channel ID; obtain it from `POST /channel/list`.

equals.description: Keys whose values must be equal on the source alert and the incoming event. Only `title`, `severity` and `labels.<name>` take effect; any other key (for example `data_source_id`) is accepted but makes the rule never fire. Must be present; an empty array also makes the rule inert.

source_filters.description: Conditions the source (inhibiting) alert must match, evaluated against active alerts already stored in the channel. Keys: `title`, `description`, `severity` (alias `incident_severity`, `alert_severity`), `status` (alias `incident_status`, `alert_status`), or any `labels.<name>`. Empty makes the rule inert.

target_filters.description: Conditions the incoming target alert event must match to be inhibited; empty means every incoming event is a target. Keys: `title`, `description`, `severity` (alias `alert_severity`, `event_severity`), `status`, `alert_key`, `title_rule`, `integration_id` (alias `data_source_id`), or any `labels.<name>`.

is_directly_discard.description: When true, matching alert events are discarded entirely; when false, alerts are still recorded but marked as muted by this rule.

CreateSilenceRuleRequest.description: Parameters for creating a silence rule. Exactly one of `time_filter` or `time_filters` must be provided, and `filters` must be non-empty.

channel_id.description: Owning channel ID; obtain it from `POST /channel/list`.

from_incident_id.description: ID of the incident this rule is created from (24-character hex). The incident must exist, and only one enabled silence rule may exist per incident.

time_filters.description: Recurring silence windows. Set exactly one of `time_filters` or `time_filter`.

time_filter.description: One-off silence window. Set exactly one of `time_filter` or `time_filters`.

filters.description: Alert event conditions (OR of AND groups); matching events are silenced while the time window is active. Required, with at least one condition. Keys: `title`, `description`, `severity` (alias `alert_severity`, `event_severity`), `status`, `alert_key`, `title_rule`, `integration_id` (alias `data_source_id`), or any `labels.<name>`.

is_directly_discard.description: When true, matching alert events are discarded entirely; when false, alerts are still recorded but marked as muted by this rule.

is_auto_delete.description: When true, a rule with a one-off `time_filter` is permanently removed about 24 hours after `end_time` (or after its last update, whichever is later). Rules created with `from_incident_id` are cleaned up the same way. Rules with recurring `time_filters` are never removed automatically. Defaults to `false`.

CreateStatusPageChangeRequest.description: Parameters for creating a status page incident or maintenance event. The first update must contain `component_changes` to define affected components; retrospective events require at least 2 updates.

page_id.description: Status page ID; obtain it from `GET /status-page/list`.

type.description: Change type: `incident` unplanned incident, `maintenance` planned maintenance.

description.description: Event description (Markdown). Must not be empty.

status.description: Initial event status. `investigating`/`identified`/`monitoring`/`resolved` apply to incidents; `scheduled`/`ongoing`/`completed` apply to maintenances.

start_at_seconds.description: Event start time in Unix seconds. Maintenances store this value as the scheduled start (with `auto_update_by_schedule`, the time the event switches to `ongoing`); when it is omitted or 0, and always for incidents, the start time is the first update's `at_seconds`.

responders.description: Member IDs responsible for the event.

linked_changes.description: Linked change IDs (related incidents, deployments, etc.).

close_at_seconds.description: Event close time in Unix seconds; must be greater than or equal to the first update's `at_seconds`. For maintenances this is the scheduled end; with `auto_update_by_schedule` the event switches to `completed` at this time, which must be within 30 days from now. For a retrospective event in a terminal status, omitting it uses the latest update's time.

items.description: One timeline update entry.

update_id.description: Update ID. Server-assigned on create; supply when replaying historical updates.

at_seconds.description: Update timestamp in Unix seconds. When omitted or 0 on the first update, defaults to the current time.

status.description:
Change status after this update. May be omitted (or null) when the overall status does not change. The first four values apply to incident-type changes, the last three to maintenance-type changes.
| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `investigating` | Investigating (incident). |
| `identified` | Root cause identified (incident). |
| `monitoring` | Fix deployed, monitoring (incident). |
| `resolved` | Resolved (incident). |
| `scheduled` | Scheduled (maintenance). |
| `ongoing` | In progress (maintenance). |
| `completed` | Completed (maintenance). |
New component status. `operational`/`degraded`/`partial_outage`/`full_outage` apply to incidents; `operational`/`under_maintenance` apply to maintenances.

component_changes.description: Component status transitions applied by this update.

updates.description: Timeline updates in non-decreasing `at_seconds` order. At least one update is required, and at least one of them must contain `component_changes`. Immediate events normally pass one update; retrospective events must pass at least 2.

notify_subscribers.description: Notify subscribers about this event. On creation one notification is sent for the last update; later timeline entries also notify while this is `true`.

auto_update_by_schedule.description: Maintenance only: automatically advance the status based on the scheduled window.

is_retrospective.description: Mark the event as retrospective (a past event recorded afterwards). Requires at least 2 entries in `updates`.

draft_id.description: ID of a draft created by `POST /status-page/draft/create` to publish with this event. The draft must be pending, target this `page_id` and `type`, and have no `change_id`; it is marked published once the event is created. Omit when not publishing a draft.

CreateStatusPageChangeTimelineRequest.description: Parameters for appending an update to a status page event timeline.

page_id.description: Status page ID; obtain it from `GET /status-page/list`.

change_id.description: Target change ID; obtain it from `GET /status-page/change/list`.

at_seconds.description: Update time in Unix seconds; must not be earlier than the event's latest timeline entry. Defaults to the current time when omitted or 0.

status.description:
Event status after this update; must be valid for the event type. Pass the current status to post an update without a status change. When moving to `resolved` or `completed`, all affected components must be back to `operational`.
| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `investigating` | Investigating (incident). |
| `identified` | Root cause identified (incident). |
| `monitoring` | Fix deployed, monitoring (incident). |
| `resolved` | Resolved (incident). |
| `scheduled` | Scheduled (maintenance). |
| `ongoing` | In progress (maintenance). |
| `completed` | Completed (maintenance). |

description.description: Update description (Markdown). Must not be empty.

status.description: New component status. `operational`/`degraded`/`partial_outage`/`full_outage` apply to incidents; `operational`/`under_maintenance` apply to maintenances.

component_changes.description: Component status transitions applied by this update. Component IDs must be unique.

draft_id.description: ID of a pending draft created by `POST /status-page/draft/create` whose `change_id` is this event; it is marked published when the update is stored. Omit when not publishing a draft.

CreateStatusPageDraftRequest.description: Parameters for storing a status page draft. The `draft` payload is stored verbatim; only the validated fields listed below are interpreted.

draft.description: Draft payload, stored verbatim (at most 64 KB serialized). The server validates the fields below and keeps any other fields unchanged for the console.

v.description: Payload format version chosen by the producer; stored, not interpreted.

page_id.description: Target status page ID; must belong to the caller's account.

page_name.description: Page name for display in the console; not validated.

type.description: Event type the draft creates or updates: `incident` unplanned incident, `maintenance` planned maintenance.

name.description: Event title, 1 to 255 characters.

message.description: Event or update description (Markdown). Must not be empty.

change_id.description: Event to append an update to; it must be an event of the same `type` on `page_id`. Omit or pass 0 to draft a new event.

status.description: Proposed event status; when set, it must be valid for `type` (`investigating`/`identified`/`monitoring`/`resolved` for incidents, `scheduled`/`ongoing`/`completed` for maintenances).

component_id.description: Component ID; must exist on the page.

name.description: Component name for display; not validated.

status.description: Proposed component status; when set, it must be valid for `type` (`operational`/`degraded`/`partial_outage`/`full_outage` for incidents, `operational`/`under_maintenance` for maintenances).

start_time.description: Scheduled start in Unix seconds, for a new maintenance.

end_time.description: Scheduled end in Unix seconds, for a new maintenance; must be greater than `start_time` when both are set.

source.description: Free-form text recording where the draft came from, such as an AI session reference; stored and shown with the draft, not interpreted. Up to 64 characters.

CreateWarRoomRequest.description: Parameters for opening an incident war room in an IM integration.

integration_id.description: IM integration ID with war room enabled; obtain it from `POST /datasource/im/war-room-enabled/list`. Feishu, DingTalk, WeCom (self-built app only), and Slack are supported.

member_ids.description: Member IDs to invite into the group; every ID must be a valid member of the account.

add_observers.description: When true, also invite members who were assigned or added as responders earlier but are no longer current responders.

DeletePostMortemRequest.description: Parameters for deleting a post-mortem report.

post_mortem_id.description: Post-mortem report ID; obtain it from `POST /incident/post-mortem/list`.

DeleteStatusPageChangeRequest.description: Parameters for deleting a status page event.

page_id.description: Status page ID; obtain it from `GET /status-page/list`.

change_id.description: Target change ID; obtain it from `GET /status-page/change/list`.

DeleteStatusPageChangeTimelineRequest.description: Parameters for deleting a timeline entry on a status page event.

page_id.description: Status page ID; obtain it from `GET /status-page/list`.

change_id.description: Owning change ID; obtain it from `GET /status-page/change/list`.

update_id.description: Timeline update ID to delete; obtain it from `GET /status-page/change/info`.

DeleteWarRoomRequest.description: Parameters for deleting an incident war room.

integration_id.description: IM integration ID; obtain it from `POST /datasource/im/war-room-enabled/list`.

unlink_only.description: When true, only remove the link between the incident and the war room without dissolving the group. Allowed only for account owners and admins, only when the IM integration is disabled or deleted, and requires `chat_id`.

chat_id.description: Chat ID of the war room to unlink, from `POST /incident/war-room/list`. Required when `unlink_only` is `true` and must match the current war room; ignored otherwise.

allOf.description: Aggregated incident + alert metrics for an account/team/channel bucket.

total_incidents_acknowledged.description: Incidents that were acknowledged at least once.

total_incidents_auto_closed.description: Incidents closed automatically because all alerts recovered.

total_incidents_escalated.description: Incidents that were escalated at least once.

total_incidents_manually_escalated.description: Incidents escalated manually at least once.

total_incidents_timeout_escalated.description: Incidents escalated on timeout at least once.

total_incidents_reassigned.description: Incidents that were reassigned at least once.

total_interruptions.description: Total interruptions: notifications sent via app push, SMS, or voice call; consecutive notifications to the same responder within 60 seconds count as one.

total_engaged_seconds.description: Total engaged time in seconds: each incident contributes the sum of close time minus acknowledgement time across its acknowledged responders.

total_seconds_to_ack.description: Total time to first acknowledgement in seconds.

total_seconds_to_close.description: Total time to close in seconds.

mean_seconds_to_ack.description: Mean time to first acknowledgement in seconds; 0 when no incident in the bucket was acknowledged.

mean_seconds_to_close.description: Mean time to close in seconds; 0 when no incident in the bucket was closed.

noise_reduction_pct.description: Noise reduction ratio (%): 100 − incidents ÷ alert events × 100, rounded to two decimals; 0 when there is no alert-event data or alert events do not exceed incidents.

acknowledgement_pct.description: Acknowledgement rate (%): acknowledged incidents ÷ total incidents × 100, rounded to two decimals and capped at 100; 0 when the bucket has no incidents.

items.description: Metric rows, newest bucket first. Buckets or dimension values without incidents produce no row; an empty array means no incidents matched.

DisableIncidentMergeRequest.description: Parameters for disabling automatic merging on incidents.

incident_ids.description: Incident IDs whose automatic merge should be disabled.

DoIncidentCustomActionRequest.description: Parameters for invoking a custom action integration on an incident.

integration_id.description: Custom action integration ID. Must be enabled and associated with the incident's channel.

DoIncidentCustomActionResponse.description: `null` when the action's HTTP request succeeded; an object with `message` when it failed.

message.description: Error returned by the HTTP request to the action's URL (for example, a timeout after 2 seconds).

DutyError.description: Error payload inside the response envelope. Present only on non-2xx responses.

message.description: Human-readable error message in the response language (`locale` / `lang` query parameter or `Accept-Language` header). May name the offending field; do not parse it.
message.example: The specified parameter template_id is not valid.

EmptyObject.description: An empty object. Returned as the `data` payload by operations whose success signal is simply the absence of an error.

EmptyResponse.description: No payload. Depending on the operation, `data` is `{}` or omitted from the envelope; rely only on the HTTP 200 status and the absence of `error`.

key.description: Event key to match on: `title`, `description`, `labels.<name>` or another alert/change event key. A `labels.<name>` key must use a valid label name.

oper.description:
Match operator.
- `IN`: matches when the key's value matches any of `vals`. A key missing from the event never matches.
- `NOTIN`: matches when the value matches none of `vals`. A key missing from the event always matches.

vals.description: Values to match (at least one). Each value is one of: an exact string; `/regex/` for a regular expression; a wildcard pattern with `*` and `?`; `cidr:<CIDR>` (e.g. `cidr:203.0.113.0/24`) for an IP range; `num:lt:<n>`, `num:le:<n>`, `num:gt:<n>` or `num:ge:<n>` for a numeric comparison.

EnrichRule.description: An enrichment rule with an optional condition and type-specific settings.

kind.description:
Rule type.
| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `extraction` | Extract a value from the alert's `title`, `description`, or a `labels.*` key via regex or GJson, and write it to a label. |
| `composition` | Render a Go `text/template` against the event and write the result to a label. |
| `mapping` | Look up labels from a mapping schema or an external mapping API. |
| `drop` | Remove the listed labels from the alert. |

if.description: Optional AND-filter list; the rule is skipped unless every filter matches. `null` when the rule has no condition. Filter keys come from the alert/change event vocabulary (e.g. `title`, `labels.severity`).

settings.description: Rule-kind–specific settings. The shape depends on `kind`.

integration_id.description: Integration ID to query enrichment rules for. Must be greater than 0.

EnrichmentItem.description: Enrichment rule set for an integration.

integration_id.description: ID of the integration this rule set belongs to; one integration has at most one rule set.

rules.description: Rules in execution order; each rule sees the labels written by the rules before it.

status.description: Rule set status: `enabled` (active) or `deleted` (soft-deleted). Read endpoints exclude soft-deleted rule sets, so responses always carry `enabled`.

creator_id.description: Creator member ID.

created_at.description: Creation timestamp, Unix seconds.

updated_at.description: Last update timestamp, Unix seconds.

deleted_at.description: Deletion time, Unix seconds. Omitted when the rule set is not deleted; read endpoints never return soft-deleted rule sets, so this is effectively always omitted.

integration_ids.description: List of integration IDs to query. Must contain at least one ID.

items.description: Enrichment rule sets.

integration_id.description: Integration ID to configure enrichment rules for.

rules.description: Ordered rule list that replaces the integration's whole rule set; send `[]` to remove all rules. Rules run in this order.

ErrorCode.description:
Error code. Every failed response sets `error.code` to one of these stable strings; branch on it rather than on the HTTP status.

| Code | HTTP | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `OK` | 200 | Reserved; never returned on a failed request. |
| `InvalidParameter` | 400 | A parameter is missing, has the wrong type, or failed validation; `message` usually names the field. |
| `BadRequest` | 400 | The request breaks a business rule or conflicts with the current state of an object; `message` says which. |
| `InvalidContentType` | 400 | The body is not sent as `application/json`. |
| `ResourceNotFound` | 400 | The referenced object does not exist in this account or was deleted. Returned as HTTP 400, not 404. |
| `NoLicense` | 400 | The account's plan does not include the feature, a plan quota is used up, the plan has expired, or credits are insufficient. |
| `ReferenceExist` | 400 | The object is still referenced by other objects, so it cannot be deleted. |
| `Unauthorized` | 401 | The APP Key is missing, invalid, or deleted. |
| `BalanceNotEnough` | 402 | Console-only (billing); not returned by Open API operations. |
| `AccessDenied` | 403 | The APP Key's permission scope or the creator's role does not allow this operation or object. |
| `RouteNotFound` | 404 | No operation matches the HTTP method and path. |
| `MethodNotAllowed` | 405 | The path exists but not for this HTTP method. |
| `UndonedOrderExist` | 409 | Console-only (billing); not returned by Open API operations. |
| `EntityTooLarge` | 413 | The request body exceeds the size limit. |
| `RequestLocked` | 423 | Console-only (sign-in protection); not returned by Open API operations. |
| `RequestVerifyRequired` | 428 | Console-only (verification code); not returned by Open API operations. |
| `DangerousOperation` | 428 | Console-only (MFA for high-risk actions); not returned by Open API operations. |
| `RequestTooFrequently` | 429 | A rate limit was hit; wait for the `Flashcat-Request-Rate-Limit-Delay` response header (seconds) before retrying. |
| `InternalError` | 500 | Unexpected server error; retry with backoff and include `request_id` when reporting. |
| `ServiceUnavailable` | 503 | A backend dependency is overloaded or unavailable; retry with backoff. |
